acousticDesorptionMechanisms.mechanism: Transient Acoustic Cavitation & Micro-Jet Boundary Disruptions
acousticDesorptionMechanisms.desorptionRole: Low frequency (28 kHz) generates massive transient cavitation bubbles that violently collapse at the membrane surface, shattering the stagnant gelatinous boundary layer and ejecting adsorbed foulants back into the bulk cross-flow with zero ceramic substrate wear.

Higher frequency (40 kHz) generates intense Schlichting streaming eddies that compress the laminar boundary layer thickness (delta) by >75%, boosting the effective mass transfer coefficient for colloidal macromolecules.

governingEquations.name: Surface Shear Rate on Rotating Ceramic Disk
governingEquations.parameters: r = local disk radius (m), N = rotational speed (RPM), ω = angular velocity (rad/s), ν = kinematic viscosity (m²/s), δ_b = boundary layer thickness (m)
governingEquations.explanation: Calculates the dynamic hydrodynamic shear rate generated directly at the rotating ceramic membrane surface. At 1500 RPM, peripheral shear rates exceed 180,000 s⁻¹, completely dislodging colloidal foulants irrespective of cross-flow pumping rate.

governingEquations.name: Darcy's Law with Acoustic Desorption & Resistance-in-Series
governingEquations.formula: J = ΔTMP / [ μ · (R_m + R_cp + R_cake - ΔR_ac) ]
governingEquations.parameters: J = permeate flux (m³/m²·s or LMH), ΔTMP = transmembrane pressure (Pa), μ = permeate dynamic viscosity (Pa·s), R_m = intrinsic membrane resistance (m⁻¹), R_cp = concentration polarization resistance, R_cake = cake layer resistance, ΔR_ac = acoustic cavitation desorption resistance mitigation (m⁻¹)
governingEquations.explanation: Quantifies the instantaneous permeate flux. Acoustic sonication (28 kHz) generates localized micro-jetting that dislodges the viscous gel cake, reducing total hydrodynamic resistance (R_cake - ΔR_ac) by up to 88%.

governingEquations.name: Primary Acoustic Radiation Force on Colloidal Particles
governingEquations.parameters: r_p = particle radius (m), ∇⟨p_ac²⟩ = gradient of time-averaged acoustic pressure squared (Pa²/m), ρ_f = fluid density (kg/m³), c = acoustic wave speed (m/s)
governingEquations.explanation: Derives the non-thermal primary acoustic radiation force propelling colloidal foulants, pectins, and cellular fragments away from the membrane face back into the bulk concentrate flow channel.

governingEquations.name: Critical Flux Boundary under High-Shear Rotation
governingEquations.parameters: J_crit = critical permeate flux below which zero fouling occurs (LMH), γ_wall = wall shear rate (s⁻¹), d_p = colloidal particle diameter (m), k_B = Boltzmann constant, C_wall/C_bulk = concentration polarization ratio
governingEquations.explanation: Defines the operating envelope where permeate drag is exactly counterbalanced by centrifugal and shear lift forces. When J < J_crit, the ceramic membrane operates indefinitely with zero decline in steady-state flux.
